slices.label: Men outside the South
slices.source: 1900 census (Twelfth Census); men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states (including declarant aliens where they could vote); turnout and choice from the backbone, calibrated to certified 1900 returns.

slices.label: Women outside the South
slices.source: 1900 census (Twelfth Census); women 21+ outside the South; women could vote for president only in Wyoming, Colorado (1893), Utah and Idaho (1896).

slices.label: White Southerners
slices.source: 1900 census (Twelfth Census); white adults in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults); calibrated to certified 1900 returns.

slices.label: Black Southerners
slices.source: 1900 census (Twelfth Census); Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; disfranchisement was intensifying (Mississippi 1890, South Carolina 1895, Louisiana's 1898 grandfather clause, North Carolina's August 1900 amendment); the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.

slices.label: Immigrants not yet citizens
slices.source: 1900 census (Twelfth Census); foreign-born white adults who were aliens or had only declared their intent (first papers); declarant aliens could vote in several Midwestern and Western states (fewer each decade as states repealed it), so part of this slice could vote.

runs.summary: Rerun with nothing changed, 1900 comes out as it did: McKinley wins, 292–155. The closest state was Kentucky, which went to Bryan by 1.7 points. Every one of my 100 reruns reproduces it exactly.
howIGotThis: The numbers: the 1900 census counts and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1900 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

south-white.name: Anna Reed
south-white.quote: I cannot vote myself, though I follow the race closely. My husband will decide how we cast our ballot tomorrow.
